description: AWS Emulator is a local emulator of the AWS APIs.

summary.one_liner: AWS Emulator is a local, no-account-needed emulator of AWS APIs for testing software without calling real AWS, runnable as a server or embedded in Rust tests.
summary.what_it_does: The emulator is a local program that serves an AWS API endpoint, with no graphical interface. In server mode you start it and set environment variables so the AWS CLI or any AWS SDK sends requests to it instead of AWS. In embedded mode you add it as a Rust dev-dependency and run one isolated instance per test, passing its HTTP client directly to the SDK client. The repository is a Cargo workspace with one crate per AWS service, each driven by a Smithy model, plus a router binary that mounts all services on one endpoint. The README says the router serves HTTPS on 127.0.0.1:9297 with a self-signed certificate. Fidelity scores against real AWS are published per release, and known gaps are tracked in an issues directory. Telemetry is on by default and can be turned off by a command-line flag, an environment variable, a config file, or the embedded API.
use_cases: test AWS SDK code without an AWS account
run AWS CLI commands against a local endpoint
integration tests in CI without calling AWS
embedded AWS mocks in Rust unit tests
develop AWS applications offline on a laptop
notable: Embedded mode runs one isolated emulator instance per Rust test with no endpoint or environment variables to set
One crate per AWS service, generated from Smithy models
Published fidelity scores per release show how closely each service matches AWS
Ships as RPM/Debian packages or a Docker container, and has an AI coding agent skill install path
Telemetry can be disabled per process, per shell, per machine, or in embedded code
caveats: Not for production workloads or security testing
Building from source is supported only on Linux (x86_64 and aarch64); Windows and macOS use Docker
Requires at least 100 GB free disk and a multi-core machine for a full build; first build is slow
The README says the repository does not accept pull requests; bugs go to GitHub Issues
